newsitem.title: USA: Freezing Midwest temperatures slow Illinois barges.
newsitem.headline: Freezing Midwest temperatures slow Illinois barges.

text.p: Two days of temperatures near zero in the northern U.S. Midwest have caused stretches of the Illinois River to freeze, bringing barge traffic nearly to a halt on Wednesday, grain dealers and river officials said.
"The Illinois River has basically shut down due to super cold conditions," one exporter said. "There is no farmer movement in corn or beans."
On Tuesday, temperatures in northern and central Illinois as of 0800 CST ranged from minus three degrees Fahrenheit to one degree, according to data from Weather Express forecasters in Omaha, Neb.
Another grain dealer on the Illinois in the central part of the state said his harbor had frozen, and only one boat had made it through early Wednesday.

"The Peoria Lake is frozen and the channel is open, but we have not seen a lot of tows this morning (Wednesday)," said Rick Granados, chief of the lock and dam section for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in Peoria.
Ice was also causing problems at the lock at Marseilles in northern Illinois, but barge operators could navigate around the lock at Peoria and LaGrange, Granados said.
At Marseilles, all tows were restricted to 105 feet in width because there is ice on the side of the lock, Granadas said. All barges on the river are also required to have ice couplings, he said.

However, forecasters expect temperatures to warm up significantly in the Midwest by the end of this weekend. In Illinois, high temperatures on Sunday were forecast to climb up to the 40s F in the north and the mid-50s in the south, according to the National Weather Service.
Several days of temperatures above freezing should melt the ice enough to get barge traffic flowing again, Granados said.
